title: In Ezekiel 5 How Does The Concept Of A Remnant Provide Hope Amidst The Severe Judgment Described In This Chapter
paragraphs: The Remnant in Ezekiel 5: Hope Amidst Judgment

Ezekiel 5 presents a vivid and sobering depiction of God’s judgment upon Jerusalem due to their persistent rebellion. The chapter uses powerful prophetic symbolism and language to communicate the seriousness of sin and the certainty of divine justice. Yet, woven into this portrayal of devastation is a thread of hope: the concept of a remnant. Let’s explore how this theme provides encouragement even in the darkest of times.
1. The Drastic Judgment on Jerusalem
The chapter opens with Ezekiel commanded to shave his head and beard, dividing the hair into three parts to symbolize the fate of Jerusalem’s inhabitants:
A third will die by plague or famine within the city
A third will fall by the sword outside the city
A third will be scattered to the wind, pursued by the sword
Therefore thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Behold, I, even I, am against thee; and I will execute judgments in the midst of thee in the sight of the nations. - Ezekiel 5:8 ASV

This severe judgment underscores God’s holiness and the seriousness with which He responds to covenant unfaithfulness. The imagery is intense and the consequences dire, reminding us that sin always has consequences (see also Romans 6:23 ASV).
2. The Glimmer of Hope: The Remnant
Amidst this prophecy of destruction, God instructs Ezekiel regarding a small portion of hair:

And thou shalt take thereof a few in number, and bind them in thy skirts. And of these again shalt thou take, and cast them into the midst of the fire, and burn them in the fire; from thence shall a fire come forth into all the house of Israel. - Ezekiel 5:3-4 ASV

This small number of hairs bound in Ezekiel’s garment represent the remnant—the small group who survive the judgment. Although a portion of these will face further hardship (“cast into the midst of the fire”), the very act of setting aside a remnant shows God’s commitment to preserve a people for Himself.
3. The Remnant: A Biblical Theme of Hope

The concept of a remnant is a recurring theme throughout Scripture, reflecting God’s faithfulness even when His people are unfaithful. Despite overwhelming judgment, God never abandons His covenant promises. Consider these examples:
God preserved Noah and his family during the flood (Genesis 6:18 ASV).
A remnant returned from Babylonian exile, as prophesied in Isaiah (Isaiah 10:20-21 ASV).
Paul affirms that “at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace” (Romans 11:5 ASV).
This theme assures us that, even when judgment is deserved and severe, God’s grace provides a way forward for His people.
4. The Remnant and the Gospel

For believers today, the remnant points us to God’s faithfulness in Christ. Just as God preserved a faithful few in Ezekiel’s day, He preserves all who place their faith in Jesus. The ultimate hope for the remnant is fulfilled in Christ, who bore our judgment so that we might be reconciled to God:
For by grace have ye been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God. - Ephesians 2:8 ASV
The hope of the remnant is the hope of the gospel: God’s mercy triumphs over judgment for all who trust in Him.
5. Living as God’s Remnant Today

Those who follow Christ are called to live as His faithful people in a world that often stands opposed to Him. The reality of judgment should sober us, but the reality of hope in Christ should empower us to faithfulness, knowing:
The Lord knoweth them that are his. - 2 Timothy 2:19 ASV
As God kept a remnant in Ezekiel’s day, He keeps His people today—assuring us of His steadfast love and ultimate victory.
